Pressure-sensitive mat · thesis baseline and V3

PSM Board Viewer

Two generations of the instrumented car-seat pressure mat: a 4×4 VCNL4020 baseline and a modular VCNL4030X01 tile/hub revision. Browse the copper, silkscreen, and full schematics below.

Schematics, layouts and checks are complete. No board has been fabricated or tested.

Signal chain

How it works

The PSM is a passive sensor array: the host selects a mux channel, reads the proximity sensor, and turns the pressure map into occupancy, posture, and respiration signals.

PSM V1 · 16 sensors, two muxes
HOST

Tiva / LaunchPad or Raspberry Pi

3V3, GND, SDA, SCL, INT_N, MUX_RST on a 2×5 header.

→
U17 / U18 · PCA9548A

Two 8-channel muxes

0x70 and 0x71. One channel per sensor because every VCNL4020 is at 0x13.

→
U1–U16 · VCNL4020

4×4 proximity array

IR proximity through the silicone domes; 25.4 mm pitch.

→
OUTPUT

Pressure map

Occupancy, posture, movement, and respiration-rate experiments.

PSM V3 · 16 sensors, one mux, four tiles
HOST

Raspberry Pi / ESP32 / Tiva

Same 2×5 host pinout as V1.

→
U1 · PCA9548A

One hub mux

0x70. Channels 0–3 go to four tile ports; channels 4–7 are spare.

→
4 tiles × 4 VCNL4030X01

Addressable tiles

Each tile has 0x60/0x51/0x40/0x41, so one mux channel reads four sensors.

→
OUTPUT

Pressure map

Modular tiles follow the car-seat contour and can be replaced individually.

The boards only implement the pressure modality. The camera, app, and alert pipeline are separate subsystems in the proposal.

Status

Checks and open questions

No board has been built. These are the design-file checks that pass, and the things only a fabricated board can answer.

Checked on the design

  • ERC: 0 violations on the V1, V3 tile, and V3 hub schematics.
  • DRC: 0 violations and 0 unconnected items on all three PCBs.
  • Schematic vs PCB: 0 pad/net mismatches.
  • Fabrication outputs: Gerbers, drill, position files, BOMs, and PDF/SVG previews are generated.
  • Libraries: custom VCNL4020/VCNL4030X01 footprints and a shared PSM symbol library are included.

Only a real board can answer

  • Does every mux channel and sensor address respond on the first power-up?
  • Is the pressure response linear and repeatable after the silicone is bonded?
  • Does the flex survive repeated bending and connector insertion?
  • Does the tile/hub fit the car-seat contour and harness without changing fit?
  • Does the full system meet the proposal's accuracy, latency, and false-alarm targets?

Not certified. These are research prototypes. They are not medical devices and are not certified to CMVSS 213.1. Do not use them with an infant in a vehicle until the mechanical fit, electrical safety, and sensor performance have been validated.
